key_insight: Patch-aligned features from foundation models (e.g., BLIP2) are highly redundant (~90% redundancy); randomly selecting a subset of patches during training (stochastic patch selection) reduces redundancy and yields better out-of-distribution generalization for end-to-end driving policies.
problem_solved: Reduces over-reliance on massively redundant patch-level features that hurt OOD robustness and increase compute for end-to-end autonomous driving models.
method: Quantify redundancy in foundation-model patch descriptors using PCA and cross-patch similarity (≈90% redundancy).
Introduce stochastic patch selection: sample a smaller subset of patch-aligned features during training instead of using all patches.
Train end-to-end driving policies on the reduced patch set to improve generalization and efficiency without changing the backbone.
impact: Enables more robust, compute-efficient end-to-end driving systems that generalize better to new environments; offers a simple, model-agnostic way for practitioners to leverage foundation-model features while avoiding redundancy-induced overfitting.
visual_elements: Bar chart / scree plot showing PCA explained variance with a marker at the ~90% redundancy point.
Schematic comparing full-patch pipeline vs stochastic patch selection pipeline (fewer patches → same or better OOD performance).
Heatmap or matrix of cross-patch similarity highlighting high redundancy across patches.
Performance plot comparing in-distribution vs OOD metrics for baseline (all patches) and proposed method (stochastic selection).
paper_title: See Less, Drive Better: Generalizable End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Foundation Models Stochastic Patch Selection
paper_authors: Amir Mallak, Erfan Aasi, Shiva Sreeram, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Daniela Rus
